scholarships.title: KAUST Fellowship (Master's, Ph.D. and M.S./Ph.D. Pathway)
scholarships.official_source: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)

existing.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.
eligibility: Bachelors degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Master's programs

Masters degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programs; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared
At least 18 years of age on entry
Minimum permitted GPA of 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent); typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3 and 75% above 3.5
Evidence of proficiency in the English language
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject for Master's entry or a relevant master's degree for Ph.D. entry, be at least 18 years old on entry, hold a minimum 3.0/4.0 GPA, and demonstrate English proficiency.
benefits: Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, which will be subject to an additional fee
Relocation assistance covers each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation
Over 90% of admitted students receive full tuition support, a monthly stipend, housing, medical coverage and relocation assistance
coverage: Full tuition and bench fee coverage (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year)
Monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 for Ph.D. students)
Base accommodation (shared accommodation for single students; 2-bed accommodation for married students)
Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs
requirements: Submit an application through the KAUST online application portal before the published round deadline
Provide contact details of 3 referees with academic or professional email addresses; personal email addresses are not accepted
Provide an official English language test score if available
Provide a clear, unobscured copy of the passport page showing picture and personal details (Saudi applicants may provide a national ID card)
All supporting documents, including academic transcripts, must be in English
If your official transcript is not in English, upload both the original transcript in the native language and a certified English translation
A statement of purpose of approximately 750 words
GRE or PGAT scores may be submitted but are not a compulsory requirement
documents: Official university transcripts (complete academic record showing courses, credits where applicable, grades, final grade or award, and the grading scale used)
Official English language test score (if available)
Clear, unobscured copy of the passport page (or national ID card for Saudi applicants)
Certified English translation of non-English transcripts
Final official transcript sent directly by the awarding institution before arrival, if admitted
existing.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107; TOEFL Home Edition accepted), or PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. Scores valid for two years from the test date.
application_method: Log into the KAUST application portal and submit the application before the published round deadline
Upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, English test score and passport page as part of the online application
Enter 3 referees' contact details, which sends reference requests to them automatically
Respond to any invitation for an online interview with KAUST faculty from your subject area
Await the decision notification by email within the published notification window for the round
existing.selection_notes: Five-stage process: submission, Admissions team document review, faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants with shortlisting for interviews, academic interview and/or test, then decision. Admission review is holistic, considering academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community. All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered, and KAUST states it cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications.
existing.best_fit: Graduate students in science, engineering, mathematics and related fields who hold a relevant bachelor's (Master's entry) or relevant master's (Ph.D. entry) degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0 and clear research interests.
existing.notes: Relocation assistance is only for each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation. Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship. Eligible students who request a housing upgrade pay an additional fee. An English proficiency score is not required if the applicant's degree was completed by in-person study at an accredited institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or if the applicant previously completed a degree taken at KAUST's campus in Thuwal; distance learning, satellite campuses, joint programs and branch institutions outside those countries do not qualify for the exemption. Applicants may submit without an English score but must meet the minimum before enrolment. Saudi nationals and PhD students scoring IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first year. KAUST does not accept Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, or IELTS One Skill Retake results. If accepted, there is a limited time to respond to secure the place or the decision may be withdrawn.
existing.duration: M.S. is a 36-credit program expected to be completed in three semesters and one summer session; the M.S./Ph.D. pathway typically takes five to six years
existing.application_period: Fall 2027 Round 2 applications open 28 September 2026 and close 3 January 2027; Spring 2027 entry (PhD only) had a Round 1 deadline of 27 September 2026 with decisions on 8 November 2026
